rule.rule: hard gates, then smallest K within one SE of best balanced silhouette
rule.qualitative_rule: candidate must be marked qualitative_preservation=true and undersegmentation=false; then apply numeric hard gates and the one-SE/smallest-K rule

criteria: Preserve visually distinct neutral macro-phenotypes without requiring every subdivision to define a new macroregion.
Separate blank, background, and section-edge appearances from pale low-cellularity tissue.
Retain cellular variation reproduced across anonymized Slides A-D, assessed using centroid, per-slide, mid/random, and low-margin exemplars together with anonymous spatial maps and composition plots.
metadata.review_scope: Blinded technical visual review of candidate K=3 through K=9 using only the anonymized exemplar atlases, spatial heatmaps, composition plots, lineage/summary visuals, and internal candidate metrics supplied for this run.
metadata.blinding_limitation: Only anonymized run materials were reviewed. This is a technical non-pathologist assessment based on neutral visual morphology and is not a diagnostic interpretation.

candidates.qualitative_notes: C0 is a broad purple cellular class represented on Slides A-D, while the visually rounder or more uniformly cellular C1 is confined to Slides B and D. C2 combines nearly empty/background fields, linear section-edge appearances, and pale sparsely cellular tissue in its centroid, per-slide, and mid/random examples; its low-margin examples also extend back into cellular tissue. The spatial maps place this mixed C2 class both along rims and through pale internal regions. Blank/edge appearance and pale low-cellularity tissue are therefore not preserved as separate neutral macro-phenotypes, and cellular variation is compressed into too few classes.

C0 and C1 provide a reproducible cellular split across Slides A-D, and C2 captures a further cellular appearance on Slides B and D. However, C3 still pools nearly blank fields, linear or abrupt section edges, pale fibrous-looking areas, and sparsely cellular tissue across centroid, per-slide, mid/random, and low-margin examples. Its spatial distribution forms both outer rims and broad internal pale regions. The principal blank/edge versus pale low-cellularity distinction remains merged despite improved cellular separation.

K=5 introduces a visually useful separation: C3 is predominantly pale eosinophilic, low-cellularity tissue with coherent regions on Slides C and D, whereas C4 is dominated by near-background, abrupt section-edge, and very sparse boundary appearances and occurs on all four slides. Some overlap remains among low-margin boundary examples, as expected at interfaces, but the centroid and mid/random sets support the distinction. C0 and C1 retain two cellular appearances represented on Slides A-D, with C2 preserving an additional cellular appearance reproduced on Slides B and D. The anonymous spatial maps show coherent rather than purely speckled regions for these classes.

C5 is a near-empty background class with consistently almost blank centroid and per-slide examples from Slides A-D. C4 retains sparse tissue and section-edge/interface structure, while C3 retains pale low-cellularity tissue concentrated in coherent regions on Slides C and D. Thus pure background, tissue boundary, and pale low-cellularity appearances are no longer forced together. C0 and C1 remain cellular classes reproduced across all four slides, and C2 preserves the additional cellular appearance on Slides B and D; their spatial maps form contiguous zones with plausible transitions.

The background hierarchy remains visually intact: C6 is almost blank on Slides A-D, C5 contains sparse tissue and section-edge/interface structure on all four slides, and C4 contains pale low-cellularity tissue with coherent representation on Slides C and D. Cellular appearances are also retained: C0 and C2 are represented across Slides A-D, C1 is reproduced on three slides, and C3 is reproduced on Slides B and D. The added cellular subdivision need not constitute a new macroregion to be acceptable; exemplar consistency, composition, and spatial coherence show that K=7 still preserves the neutral macro-phenotypes without evident undersegmentation.

C7 remains an almost blank background class across Slides A-D; C6 contains section-edge/interface and very sparse tissue on all four slides; and C5 contains a paler low-cellularity tissue appearance concentrated on Slides C and D. These are distinguishable in centroid, per-slide, and mid/random examples despite expected mixing in low-margin examples. Among cellular tissue, C0, C2, and C3 each recur across Slides A-D and occupy structured spatial zones, while C1 and C4 retain reproducible multi-slide variants. K=8 therefore preserves the required macro-level distinctions while allowing finer cellular subdivision.

C8 is an almost blank background class represented on Slides A-D. C7 retains section-edge, pale boundary, and very sparse tissue appearances across the four slides, while C6 retains a pale low-cellularity tissue class on Slides C and D; C5 adds a less-dense elongated-cellular appearance reproduced across Slides A-D. C0, C2, and C3 are also cellular classes represented on all four slides, with C1 and C4 providing additional multi-slide variants. The spatial maps and composition plot support preservation of the main neutral distinctions, although several adjacent cellular classes overlap in low-margin examples and the supplied internal repeatability metrics are weaker at K=9 than at lower K.
